capability.problem: Identify whether a paid catalyst write changes subsequent fresh-feed processing and yields useful isolated product under a reproducible common read/reset operation.
capability.current_best: Acquired Wang Chem2026 article/SI reports continuous selective acetylene removal; 200-hour stability at2sccm and100sccm two-cell purification are distinct regimes. Generic carbon-isotope/SSITKA attribution is established.
capability.limitation: Optimum-waveform work, raw chromatograms, complete fresh-cohort fate and calibrated common-regime exposure remain unavailable. Electronic and hidden-H/transport mechanisms are not distinguished.
capability.proposed_mechanism: Randomize pulse/sham before admitting a fresh carbon-labelled feed cohort, then impose identical mixed-feed readout and a complete chase with distinct acetylene/ethylene tags.

target.metric: lower simultaneous-error bound on changed fresh-cohort chemical fate and retained useful product per fully paid restored operation
target.unit: moles and product purity/recovery, plus joules and resources per isolated useful product
target.conditions: Same specimen/feed/exposure and waveform; complete tag/fate and missing-product bounds; target numerical acceptance threshold frozen before new measurement.
target.comparator: Same feed/output specification and full solvent, energy, reset and lifetime boundary against static/dynamic catalyst and acquired continuous electrochemical incumbents.

scientific_evidence.judgement: Primary workbooks acquired and conditional causal theorem internally derived
scientific_evidence.limits: No new intervention or retained-state operation executed.

feasibility_and_readiness.limits: Fresh-cohort common-read/chase, calibration, optimum switching work and product/reset gates are open.

next_step_value.judgement: Decisive acquisition before mechanism or waveform promotion
next_step_value.limits: Excludes old-product purge only under complete fate/exposure assumptions; electronic identity needs a further distinguishing intervention.
